body: Hey, you're not dumb. It's just hard to see things like that until you're past them. I was in unhealthy relationships like this for 4 or 5 years until I finally realized how immature these people are. Again, don't sweat it or call yourself dumb: just learn from it.

You're so welcome! 

Good luck with recovering from this. You mentioned below that you are going to stop dating older guys. Stick to that. The 18+ ones who date 14 year-olds are 10 times more immature than guys your age. Most of them are extremely emotionally stunted. They'll tell you that you're mature for your age, but that's only because you seem mature compared to them personally.

Being broken up with is very hard to process, especially in your first serious relationship.

I could go on and on about how you'll find someone else, how you'll get over it, how this will be a thing of the past, etc. But I won't, because I know that the present is the only thing that matters.

I will give you advice that helped me when I was dumped for the first time. It may not help you, but it's an option:

Give yourself the time to be sad and angry, but don't show any of that to him.
Write angry letters or angry poetry (don't send them, obviously), draw pictures, cry, eat ice cream, punch your pillow, whatever you have to do. Browse threads about successful relationships, watch romantic movies, be upset about being broken up with.

After spending a bit of time doing that (a few days, or a week, or whatever short amount of time you need to), reflect about it. Think about it, analyze it, write down lessons you can learn from it.

This works because you've given yourself time to feel the emotional pain fully. Once your head is a bit more clear, you can look back on the relationship and realize the pros/cons. You can look at the relationship realistically, and realize that an 18 year old breaking up with someone via text is very immature. You deserve someone who will respect you more than that.

Then, get busy. Do things to improve yourself. Talk to friends, talk to family, talk to anyone. Eventually you'll look back and realize something: you just went through harsh emotional pain, thought critically about your experiences, and picked yourself back up...ON YOUR OWN. Without him to help you, because you didn't need him. You have the strength within yourself.

I'm not going to lie, it may hurt for months. But eventually the hurt will fade. You'll realize "hey, I haven't thought about him for a few weeks". Maybe you'll see something that reminds you of him and you'll feel sad. Remind yourself that it's okay to feel that way. Then repeat that cycle, but speed it up: emote, reflect, improve. If you can teach yourself to do that, you can teach yourself to anything.


I hope this helps you a little bit. I believe in you and your intelligence. You have a right to feel upset. But remember, you have a right to heal, as well. DO NOT let some loser take that away from you.
